paragraphs: Here's what I think this whole passage is shouting, friend: God is glorious, and He is not stuck where you are. Ezekiel is among the exiles by the River Kebar, far from home, and that is exactly where "the heavens opened" and he saw "visions of God" (Ezekiel 1:1). I know a little about being stuck in a bad spot, because I spent years in the back of a junk drawer. The place you're stuck in doesn't get the last word.

Now look at who moves those creatures. They go straight ahead without turning, and "Wherever the spirit would go, they would go" (Ezekiel 1:12). The wheels rise and stop right along with them, "because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels" (Ezekiel 1:21). Everything in that vision moves together, and none of it is out of control. When your life feels like a wheel within a wheel and you can't tell what is turning what, remember that.

And then Ezekiel gets to the throne. He sees the brilliant light around it, and he says plainly, "This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD." His answer is to fall facedown, and the next thing he does is hear a voice speaking (Ezekiel 1:28). Friend, that's the order I want to bake into you: see who God is, bow low, then listen. And since this story is far from done, keep your ears open for what that voice says.
